summary:
Gombe State criminalises same-sex conduct under its own Sharia Penal Code Law 2001, signed into law on 23 November 2001, which operates alongside federal law. Human Rights Watch's 2004 survey of Shari'a implementation lists Gombe among the twelve northern states that had adopted Shari'a into criminal legislation by 2002, with Shari'a courts holding criminal jurisdiction over Muslims beyond the federal code.

The penalties are severe and gendered. Gombe, Jigawa, Kano and Zamfara share a sodomy offence that punishes unmarried men with 100 lashes plus one year's imprisonment and married men with stoning to death (rajm). The offence covering same-sex conduct between women carries up to 50 lashes plus up to six months' imprisonment. Gombe defines gross indecency in its own formulation as 'any sexual offence against the normal or usual standards of behaviour'. The enacted statutory text reaches same-sex conduct by men and women beyond the federal code.

Gombe enforces its moral-crimes layer on the ground. In October 2023 the Gombe State Command of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps raided a birthday gathering at Duwa Plaza along the Bauchi-Gombe Expressway where a same-sex wedding was being prepared, arresting 76 people. State PRO Buhari Sa'ad told reporters that 59 males were detained, 21 of whom confessed to being homosexuals, with 17 females present at the scene, and that those arrested would be charged to court for 'a crime in Gombe State'.

The Guardian of Lagos, in a report bylined James Agberebi and archived on 4 December 2023, independently confirms the raid: about 76 people were arrested after a tip-off about a same-sex birthday party and planned marriage. Gombe NSCDC Commandant Mohammed Muazu confirmed the arrests; spokesperson Buhari Saad said 21 of the 59 detained males were involved in gay activities while the remaining males and the 17 females were invited guests and onlookers, and officers voiced concern over the participants' ages.

The Sharia layer within which Gombe's statute sits is assessed in the UK Home Office country policy and information note of June 2025, which records that Islamic law applies to Muslims in the twelve northern states and includes a dedicated section on enforcement of Sharia provisions and the attitude of the hisbah (morality police).
tangentialFactors:
Gombe's sodomy provision is not unique in the north: Jigawa, Kano and Zamfara share the same formulation, punishing unmarried men with 100 lashes and one year's imprisonment and married men with stoning to death.

The UK Home Office assessment of June 2025 records that penalties for same-sex acts between women across the twelve northern states range from death to flogging and imprisonment, a wider range than Gombe's own statutory maximum of 50 lashes and six months.

Documentation of Gombe's Shari'a adoption runs from Human Rights Watch's 2004 listing to the UK Home Office assessment of June 2025; no source in the inventory records amendment or repeal of the 2001 statute.
localsOnly:
Residents of Gombe face the state's own penal code in addition to federal law, and the state's definition of gross indecency is broad enough to reach conduct the federal code does not.

The October 2023 raid at Duwa Plaza shows that private social gatherings are targets: 76 people were arrested, and the state's account distinguishes only 21 of the 59 detained males as having confessed to homosexual activity, with the remaining men and all 17 women described as invited guests and onlookers. Attendance at such an event carries exposure to arrest and local charging.

Officers at the raid voiced concern over the ages of those detained, indicating that young people were among the 76 arrested.
outOfScopeNotes:
The disposition of the October 2023 Gombe arrests is unresolved in the sources: whether the 21 who confessed, or any of the others, were charged, tried or convicted is not recorded.

No source in the inventory records a conviction under Gombe's Sharia Penal Code Law 2001 for same-sex conduct; the enforcement evidence is the arrest and the stated intent to charge.

Whether Gombe operates a hisbah with the enforcement posture described in the UK assessment is not separately sourced for Gombe.

The claim that Shari'a courts in Gombe hold criminal jurisdiction over Muslims beyond federal law rests on the 2004 Human Rights Watch listing; no later source in the inventory re-examines it.
